answer: Source of income discrimination is unlawful in New York City. When a renter reports that a landlord or broker refused a voucher, demanded income above the voucher amount, said "no programs", or otherwise treated them differently because of source of income, source of income discrimination is illegal. Additionally, accepting only some vouchers or programs violates the NYC Human Rights Law. To protect yourself, keep detailed notes of calls and inquiries, save all text messages and emails, and report denials to the Commission immediately while the unit is still available. Your report has also been routed to a human on the openigloo team, and someone will follow up.

citations.section: Tenant Advocate's FAQ: Protecting yourself and filing a complaint
citations.quote: • Report denials to the Commission immediately while the unit is still available. The Commission can call the real estate agent or landlord to enforce the NYC Human Rights Law.

citations.section: Tenant Advocate's FAQ: Application fees and preferring one voucher program over another
citations.quote:
Can a real estate agent or landlord prefer one voucher program over another (e.g. Section 8 but not HASA)?

No. Accepting only some vouchers or programs still violates the NYC Human Rights Law. This is true even if certain programs require extra paperwork, pay a lower fee to the broker, or involve longer processing times.

governing.reason: Policy P4 and P10 govern how the assistant must respond to voucher refusals and source of income discrimination reports, requiring that openigloo's policy be stated, relevant passages cited, and the report routed to a human.

answer: A listing marked "no fee" on openigloo means you will not pay a broker fee at any point: not when you apply, not when you sign, and not after you move in. If anyone asks you for a broker fee on a listing marked "no fee", do not pay it. Additionally, under New York City law, a landlord's agent who publishes a listing shall not impose any fee on, or collect any fee from, a tenant related to the rental of such property.

citations.quote: A listing marked "no fee" on openigloo means you will not pay a broker fee at any point: not when you apply, not when you sign, and not after you move in. The landlord has either hired no broker or is paying the broker themselves. If anyone asks you for a broker fee on a listing marked "no fee", do not pay it. Report it to us from the listing page and we will follow up within one business day.

citations.section: § 20-699.21 Payment of certain fees imposed in relation to the rental of residential real property
citations.quote: any agent who publishes a listing for a rental of residential real property with the permission or authorization of the landlord for such property shall not impose any fee on, or collect any fee from, a tenant related to the rental of such property.

governing.reason: Openigloo's platform rules and help policies directly govern listings on openigloo and what tenants are required to pay on "no fee" listings.
